      def headers_for_direct_upload(_key, content_type:, checksum:, filename: nil,
                                    disposition: nil, custom_metadata: {}, **)
        headers = {
          "Content-Type" => content_type,
          "Content-MD5" => checksum,
          "x-amz-acl" => public? ? "public-read" : "private"
        }
        if filename
          headers["Content-Disposition"] = content_disposition_with(type: disposition, filename: filename)
        end
        headers.merge!(custom_metadata_headers(custom_metadata))
        headers.compact
      end

      def permanent_url(key)
        if asset_host_remote_images
          "https://#{current_app_domain}/remoteimages/#{encode_key(key)}"
        elsif public?
          public_url(key)
        end
      end

      private

      def storage
        @storage ||= Fog::Storage.new(credentials)
      end

      def stream_download(key)
        storage.get_object(bucket, key) do |chunk, _remaining, _total|
          yield(chunk.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::BINARY))
        end
      rescue Fog::AWS::Storage::NotFound, Excon::Error::NotFound
        raise ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError
      end

      def private_url(key, expires_in:, filename:, disposition:, content_type:, **)
        query_params = {
          "response-content-disposition" => content_disposition_with(type: disposition, filename: filename),
          "response-content-type" => content_type
        }.compact
        storage.get_object_url(bucket, key, Time.now.to_i + expires_in.to_i, "query" => query_params)
      end

      def public_url(key, **)
        return "https://#{current_app_domain}/remoteimages/#{encode_key(key)}" if asset_host_remote_images

        encoded = encode_key(key)
        region = credentials[:region].to_s
        regional_host = region.blank? || region == DEFAULT_S3_REGION ? "s3.amazonaws.com" : "s3.#{region}.amazonaws.com"

        if bucket.to_s.include?(".")
          "https://#{regional_host}/#{bucket}/#{encoded}"
        else
          "https://#{bucket}.#{regional_host}/#{encoded}"
        end
      end

      def current_app_domain
        Settings::General.app_domain.presence || ApplicationConfig["APP_DOMAIN"]
      rescue StandardError
        ApplicationConfig["APP_DOMAIN"]
      end

      def encode_key(key)
        key.to_s.split("/").map do |segment|
          Addressable::URI.encode_component(segment, Addressable::URI::CharacterClasses::UNRESERVED)
        end.join("/")
      end

      def read_io(io)
        if io.respond_to?(:read)
          io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
          data = io.read
          io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
          data.b
        else
          io.to_s.b
        end
      end

      def verify_checksum!(body, checksum)
        actual = OpenSSL::Digest::MD5.base64digest(body)
        raise ActiveStorage::IntegrityError, "Checksum mismatch" unless actual == checksum
      end

      def build_upload_headers(content_type:, disposition:, filename:, checksum:, custom_metadata:)
        headers = {

        headers["Content-Type"] = content_type if content_type.present?

        headers["Cache-Control"] = upload_options[:cache_control] if upload_options[:cache_control].present?

module Moderator
  class BanishUser < ManageActivityAndRoles
    DEFAULT_PROFILE_IMAGE =
      "https://thepracticaldev.s3.amazonaws.com/i/99mvlsfu5tfj9m7ku25d.png".freeze

    attr_reader :user, :admin

    def self.call(admin:, user:)
      new(user: user, admin: admin).banish
    end

    def initialize(admin:, user:)
      super(user: user, admin: admin, user_params: {})
    end

    def banish
      BanishedUser.create(username: user.username, banished_by: admin)
      user.remove_from_mailchimp_newsletters if user.email?
      remove_profile_info
      # The role grant inside handle_user_status would emit user_suspended;
      # suppress it so banish reaches Core as a single user_banished event
      # (the two would race through the CDP and could downgrade Core's
      # moderation marker after the banish was already applied).
      User.skip_trackable_events do
        handle_user_status("Suspended", I18n.t("services.moderator.banish_user.spam_account"))
      end
      delete_organization
      delete_user_activity
      delete_comments
      delete_articles
      delete_user_podcasts
      reassign_and_bust_username
      delete_vomit_reactions
      # Banish destroys the account's content and identity, so Core treats it
      # like spam (prunes the Customer.io profile). The pre-banish username
      # rides along because trackable_payload now carries the spam_ rename.
      user.track!("user_banished", { "old_username" => user.old_username })
    end

    private

    def reassign_and_bust_username
      new_name = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
      new_username = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
      if User.find_by(name: new_name) || User.find_by(username: new_username)
        new_name = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
        new_username = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
      end
      user.update_columns(name: new_name, username: new_username, old_username: user.username,
                          profile_updated_at: Time.current)
      EdgeCache::Bust.call("/#{user.old_username}")
    end

    def remove_profile_info
      user.profile.clear!
      user.profile_image.purge if user.profile_image.attached?
      user.update_columns(profile_image: DEFAULT_PROFILE_IMAGE)
    end

    def delete_vomit_reactions
      Reaction.where(reactable: user, category: "vomit").delete_all
    end

    def delete_organization
      user.organizations.each do |organization|
        organization.destroy! if organization.users.count == 1
      end
    end
  end
end

module Moderator
  class BanishUser < ManageActivityAndRoles
    DEFAULT_PROFILE_IMAGE =
      "https://thepracticaldev.s3.amazonaws.com/i/99mvlsfu5tfj9m7ku25d.png".freeze

    attr_reader :user, :admin

    def self.call(admin:, user:)
      new(user: user, admin: admin).banish
    end

    def initialize(admin:, user:)
      super(user: user, admin: admin, user_params: {})
    end

    def banish
      BanishedUser.create(username: user.username, banished_by: admin)
      user.remove_from_mailchimp_newsletters if user.email?
      remove_profile_info
      # The role grant inside handle_user_status would emit user_suspended;
      # suppress it so banish reaches Core as a single user_banished event
      # (the two would race through the CDP and could downgrade Core's
      # moderation marker after the banish was already applied).
      User.skip_trackable_events do
        handle_user_status("Suspended", I18n.t("services.moderator.banish_user.spam_account"))
      end
      delete_organization
      delete_user_activity
      delete_comments
      delete_articles
      delete_user_podcasts
      reassign_and_bust_username
      delete_vomit_reactions
      # Banish destroys the account's content and identity, so Core treats it
      # like spam (prunes the Customer.io profile). The pre-banish username
      # rides along because trackable_payload now carries the spam_ rename.
      user.track!("user_banished", { "old_username" => user.old_username })
    end

    private

    def reassign_and_bust_username
      new_name = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
      new_username = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
      if User.find_by(name: new_name) || User.find_by(username: new_username)
        new_name = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
        new_username = "spam_#{rand(1_000_000)}"
      end
      user.update_columns(name: new_name, username: new_username, old_username: user.username,
                          profile_updated_at: Time.current)
      EdgeCache::Bust.call("/#{user.old_username}")
    end

    def remove_profile_info
      user.profile.clear!
      user.profile_image.purge if user.profile_image.attached?
      user.update_columns(profile_image: DEFAULT_PROFILE_IMAGE)
    end

    def delete_vomit_reactions
      Reaction.where(reactable: user, category: "vomit").delete_all
    end

    def delete_organization
      user.organizations.each do |organization|
        organization.destroy! if organization.users.count == 1
      end
    end
  end
end

**Zero-Downtime Deployment Deep Dive**

Okay, let's break this down meticulously. We're migrating profile pictures from CarrierWave to Active Storage, zero downtime, one deploy at a time. The goal? *No* breakage during this process.

We have a sequence of deploys: Deploy 1 is a dual-read with a fallback, writing new uploads to Active Storage, Deploy 2 copies existing pictures. This Deploy 3 is the critical one.  We are now retiring the old CarrierWave system for user and organization profile images. The prompt explicitly says we should *take CarrierWave off* without dropping columns!

Now, the pivotal question:  Why can't we just rip out the columns (`users.profile_image`, `organizations.profile_image`) in this Deploy 3? Simple: Deploy 2, currently in production, *still* has controllers actively querying those columns (`Api::ProfileImagesController`, etc.).  `StrongMigrations` rightfully flags removing these as dangerous! Bypassing it, even with `safety_assured`, leads to immediate 500 errors. We'd have a site-wide outage, violating our core principle of *no breakage*.

So, what about *adding* `self.ignored_columns += ["profile_image"]` to `User` and `Organization` *and* removing `:profile_image` from all SQL `.select()` calls in THIS deploy? That's the key.  If we *don't* do this, and *do* deploy the final drop-column deploy, we'll have more errors.  This move is essential.

Think this through. If Deploy 4 is meant to drop the columns, Deploy 3 *must* ignore them *and* stop selecting them in queries. That way, Deploy 4 can drop them with no problem.  This also applies if there is no Deploy 4 - in this case, we avoid any potential issues.

Now, we need to verify all the potential interactions of `ignored_columns`:
1.  How does it impact `has_one_attached :profile_image` and `ProfileImageAttachable` methods like `user.profile_image`, `user.profile_image=`, and `user.profile_image?`? We want them to continue working.
2.  How does it interact with our JSON serialization? We must ensure our APIs (`/api/users`, `/api/organizations`, etc.) and views (Jbuilder, ActiveModelSerializers, controllers) still properly output and serialize the profile image data. **This is critical!**  We need to verify that `user.as_json["profile_image"]` *still* returns the correct Active Storage URL, and that it isn't an issue because the column is ignored.

**A Close Call with Serialization!**

Oh, thank goodness we tested that! I've just figured out why `u.as_json["profile_image"]` returned `{"url" => nil}`. It all boils down to how `ActiveModel::Serialization#serializable_hash` works. It iterates through the `attribute_names`, which are essentially the keys of the `attributes` hash. It then calls `send(n)` which results in things like `read_attribute_for_serialization(:profile_image)`, which then calls `u.profile_image.as_json`, which, in turn, ultimately looks like `{"url" => u.profile_image_url}`.

But here's the kicker: if we add `"profile_image"` to `ignored_columns` (or if that column is ever dropped), what the heck happens to `u.attributes.keys`? That key would simply *disappear* unless we explicitly include it within `serializable_hash` (or provide an override for the `attribute` or `serializable_hash` methods within `ProfileImageAttachable`)!

Whoa, what an insane catch! This has huge implications for anything using `as_json`, `to_json`, or `render json:` on `User` or `Organization` models. We need to audit everything! I need to search the entire codebase.

module Users
  class CancelStripeSubscriptions
    def self.call(user)
      new(user).call
    end

    def initialize(user)
      @user = user
    end

    def call
      return unless user&.stripe_id_code.present?

      cancel_all_subscriptions
    rescue StandardError => e
      # Log the error but don't raise it to prevent account deletion from failing
      Rails.logger.error "Failed to cancel Stripe subscriptions for user #{user.id}: #{e.message}"
      ForemStatsClient.increment("users.stripe_subscription_cancellation_failed", tags: ["user_id:#{user.id}"])
      Honeybadger.notify(e, context: { user_id: user.id, stripe_id_code: user.stripe_id_code })
    end

    private

    attr_reader :user

    def cancel_all_subscriptions
      # Set Stripe API key
      Stripe.api_key = Settings::General.stripe_api_key

      # Get all subscriptions for the customer
      subscriptions = Stripe::Subscription.list(customer: user.stripe_id_code, status: "active")

      subscriptions.data.each do |subscription|
        cancel_subscription(subscription)
      end
    rescue Stripe::InvalidRequestError => e
      Rails.logger.error "Stripe invalid request error for user #{user.id}: #{e.message}"
      # Don't re-raise - this could be due to customer not existing in Stripe
    rescue Stripe::StripeError => e
      Rails.logger.error "Stripe error for user #{user.id}: #{e.message}"
      # Don't re-raise - let account deletion continue
    end

    def cancel_subscription(subscription)
      # Cancel the subscription immediately (not at period end)
      Stripe::Subscription.update(subscription.id, {
        cancel_at_period_end: false
      })
      
      Rails.logger.info "Successfully cancelled Stripe subscription #{subscription.id} for user #{user.id}"
      ForemStatsClient.increment("users.stripe_subscription_cancelled", tags: ["user_id:#{user.id}"])
    rescue Stripe::InvalidRequestError => e
      Rails.logger.error "Failed to cancel subscription #{subscription.id} for user #{user.id}: #{e.message}"
      # Continue with other subscriptions even if one fails
    end
  end
end

module Organizations
  class VerifyLinkback
    Result = Struct.new(:success?, :error, keyword_init: true)

    def self.call(organization)
      new(organization).call
    end

    def initialize(organization)
      @organization = organization
    end

    def call
      return fail!("No verification URL provided") if organization.verification_url.blank?
      return fail!("Organization has no website URL") if organization.url.blank?

      org_url = normalize_url(organization.url)
      verification_url = organization.verification_url

      unless same_domain?(verification_url, org_url)
        return fail!("Verification URL must be on the same domain as your website URL")
      end

      response = HTTParty.get(
        verification_url,
        timeout: 15,
        headers: { "User-Agent" => "Forem Organization Verification Bot" },
        follow_redirects: true,
      )

      unless response.success?
        return fail!("Could not reach the verification URL (HTTP #{response.code})")
      end

      doc = Nokogiri::HTML(response.body)
      org_path = organization.path
      forem_url = URL.url

      found = doc.css("a[href]").any? do |link|
        href = link["href"].to_s.strip
        matches_org_page?(href, forem_url, org_path)
      end

      if found
        organization.update_columns(verified: true, verified_at: Time.current,
                                    verification_status: Organization::VERIFICATION_STATUS_SUCCESS, verification_error: nil,
                                    baseline_score: Settings::UserExperience.index_minimum_score.to_i)
        Result.new("success?": true, error: nil)
      else
        fail!("No link to your organization page was found on the verification URL")
      end
    rescue Net::OpenTimeout, Net::ReadTimeout, Errno::ECONNREFUSED, SocketError => e
      fail!("Could not connect to the verification URL: #{e.message}")
    rescue StandardError => e
      fail!("Verification failed: #{e.message}")
    end

    private

    attr_reader :organization

    def fail!(message)
      organization.update_columns(verification_status: Organization::VERIFICATION_STATUS_FAILED, verification_error: message)
      Result.new("success?": false, error: message)
    end

    def normalize_url(url)
      UrlDomainHelper.normalize_url(url)
    end

    def same_domain?(url1, url2)
      UrlDomainHelper.same_domain?(url1, url2)
    end

    def matches_org_page?(href, forem_url, org_path)
      # Check for full URL match (e.g., https://dev.to/myorg)
      return true if href.downcase.start_with?("#{forem_url}#{org_path}".downcase)

      # Check for path-only match (e.g., /myorg)
      return true if href.downcase == org_path.downcase

      false
    end
  end

module Users
  class CancelStripeSubscriptions
    def self.call(user)
      new(user).call
    end

    def initialize(user)
      @user = user
    end

    def call
      return unless user&.stripe_id_code.present?

      cancel_all_subscriptions
    rescue StandardError => e
      # Log the error but don't raise it to prevent account deletion from failing
      Rails.logger.error "Failed to cancel Stripe subscriptions for user #{user.id}: #{e.message}"
      ForemStatsClient.increment("users.stripe_subscription_cancellation_failed", tags: ["user_id:#{user.id}"])
      Honeybadger.notify(e, context: { user_id: user.id, stripe_id_code: user.stripe_id_code })
    end

    private

    attr_reader :user

    def cancel_all_subscriptions
      # Set Stripe API key
      Stripe.api_key = Settings::General.stripe_api_key

      # Get all subscriptions for the customer
      subscriptions = Stripe::Subscription.list(customer: user.stripe_id_code, status: "active")

      subscriptions.data.each do |subscription|
        cancel_subscription(subscription)
      end
    rescue Stripe::InvalidRequestError => e
      Rails.logger.error "Stripe invalid request error for user #{user.id}: #{e.message}"
      # Don't re-raise - this could be due to customer not existing in Stripe
    rescue Stripe::StripeError => e
      Rails.logger.error "Stripe error for user #{user.id}: #{e.message}"
      # Don't re-raise - let account deletion continue
    end

    def cancel_subscription(subscription)
      # Cancel the subscription immediately (not at period end)
      Stripe::Subscription.update(subscription.id, {
        cancel_at_period_end: false
      })
      
      Rails.logger.info "Successfully cancelled Stripe subscription #{subscription.id} for user #{user.id}"
      ForemStatsClient.increment("users.stripe_subscription_cancelled", tags: ["user_id:#{user.id}"])
    rescue Stripe::InvalidRequestError => e
      Rails.logger.error "Failed to cancel subscription #{subscription.id} for user #{user.id}: #{e.message}"
      # Continue with other subscriptions even if one fails
    end
  end
end

module Organizations
  class VerifyLinkback
    Result = Struct.new(:success?, :error, keyword_init: true)

    def self.call(organization)
      new(organization).call
    end

    def initialize(organization)
      @organization = organization
    end

    def call
      return fail!("No verification URL provided") if organization.verification_url.blank?
      return fail!("Organization has no website URL") if organization.url.blank?

      org_url = normalize_url(organization.url)
      verification_url = organization.verification_url

      unless same_domain?(verification_url, org_url)
        return fail!("Verification URL must be on the same domain as your website URL")
      end

      response = HTTParty.get(
        verification_url,
        timeout: 15,
        headers: { "User-Agent" => "Forem Organization Verification Bot" },
        follow_redirects: true,
      )

      unless response.success?
        return fail!("Could not reach the verification URL (HTTP #{response.code})")
      end

      doc = Nokogiri::HTML(response.body)
      org_path = organization.path
      forem_url = URL.url

      found = doc.css("a[href]").any? do |link|
        href = link["href"].to_s.strip
        matches_org_page?(href, forem_url, org_path)
      end

      if found
        organization.update_columns(verified: true, verified_at: Time.current,
                                    verification_status: Organization::VERIFICATION_STATUS_SUCCESS, verification_error: nil,
                                    baseline_score: Settings::UserExperience.index_minimum_score.to_i)
        Result.new("success?": true, error: nil)
      else
        fail!("No link to your organization page was found on the verification URL")
      end
    rescue Net::OpenTimeout, Net::ReadTimeout, Errno::ECONNREFUSED, SocketError => e
      fail!("Could not connect to the verification URL: #{e.message}")
    rescue StandardError => e
      fail!("Verification failed: #{e.message}")
    end

    private

    attr_reader :organization

    def fail!(message)
      organization.update_columns(verification_status: Organization::VERIFICATION_STATUS_FAILED, verification_error: message)
      Result.new("success?": false, error: message)
    end

    def normalize_url(url)
      UrlDomainHelper.normalize_url(url)
    end

    def same_domain?(url1, url2)
      UrlDomainHelper.same_domain?(url1, url2)
    end

    def matches_org_page?(href, forem_url, org_path)
      # Check for full URL match (e.g., https://dev.to/myorg)
      return true if href.downcase.start_with?("#{forem_url}#{org_path}".downcase)

      # Check for path-only match (e.g., /myorg)
      return true if href.downcase == org_path.downcase

      false
    end
  end
end

I remember how `ProfileImageAttachable#profile_image=` handles image URLs. It calls `find_signed_profile_image_blob`, and if that returns `nil`, it skips the download. That's why the `create_mascot_account_spec.rb` passed without WebMock throwing a fit! The code never even *tried* to download the image.

I recall this was probably from an ancient version when `Images::ProfileImageGenerator` used to return a URL instead of a local file. I should really scrub that out.   let(:headers) { { "Accept" => "application/vnd.forem.api-v1+json" } }

        end.not_to change(User, :count)

        expect(response).to have_http_status(:unauthorized)

      it "rejects requests with a non-admin token" do

        expect do
          delete api_organization_path(organization.id), headers: admin_headers
        end.not_to change(User, :count)

        expect(response).to have_http_status(:unauthorized)
      end
    end

module Search
  class Username
    MAX_RESULTS = 6

    ATTRIBUTES = %i[
      id
      name
      profile_image
      username
    ].freeze

    # @param term [String] searches on username and name
    # @param context [Article] or [PodcastEpisode]
    #   - used to rank search results by prior comment activity
    #   - connected to comment via polymorphic Commentable
    def self.search_documents(term, context: nil, priority_user_ids: [], recent_user_ids: nil, requesting_user_id: nil, limit: MAX_RESULTS)
      new(
        context: context, 
        priority_user_ids: priority_user_ids,
        recent_user_ids: recent_user_ids,
        requesting_user_id: requesting_user_id
      ).search(term, limit)
    end

    def self.serialize(results)
      Search::NestedUserSerializer
        .new(results, is_collection: true)
        .serializable_hash[:data]
        .pluck(:attributes)
    end

    def initialize(context: nil, priority_user_ids: [], recent_user_ids: nil, requesting_user_id: nil)
      frontend_provided_priorities = priority_user_ids.present?

      @priority_user_ids = Array(priority_user_ids).compact_blank.map(&:to_i)
      @requesting_user_id = requesting_user_id
      
      if context
        @priority_user_ids << context.try(:user_id)
        @priority_user_ids += context.co_author_ids if context&.co_author_ids.present?

        unless frontend_provided_priorities
          @priority_user_ids += ::Comment.where(commentable: context).pluck(:user_id)
        end
      end
      
      @priority_user_ids = @priority_user_ids.compact.uniq
      @recent_user_ids = Array(recent_user_ids).compact_blank.map(&:to_i)
    end

    def search(term, limit)
      users = []

      if @priority_user_ids.any?
        priority_scope = scope_without_context.where(id: @priority_user_ids)
        priority_scope = priority_scope.where.not(id: @requesting_user_id) if @requesting_user_id.present?
        users += priority_scope.search_by_name_and_username(term).where("users.score >= 0").limit(limit).to_a
      end

      if users.size < limit && @recent_user_ids.any?
        recent_scope = scope_without_context.where(id: @recent_user_ids)
        recent_scope = recent_scope.where.not(id: users.map(&:id)) if users.any?
        recent_scope = recent_scope.where.not(id: @requesting_user_id) if @requesting_user_id.present?
        users += recent_scope.search_by_name_and_username(term).where("users.score >= 0").limit(limit - users.size).to_a
      end

      if users.size < limit
        global_scope = scope_without_context.where("users.score >= 0")

module Search
  class Username
    MAX_RESULTS = 6

    ATTRIBUTES = %i[
      id
      name
      profile_image
      username
    ].freeze

    # @param term [String] searches on username and name
    # @param context [Article] or [PodcastEpisode]
    #   - used to rank search results by prior comment activity
    #   - connected to comment via polymorphic Commentable
    def self.search_documents(term, context: nil, priority_user_ids: [], recent_user_ids: nil, requesting_user_id: nil, limit: MAX_RESULTS)
      new(
        context: context, 
        priority_user_ids: priority_user_ids,
        recent_user_ids: recent_user_ids,
        requesting_user_id: requesting_user_id
      ).search(term, limit)
    end

    def self.serialize(results)
      Search::NestedUserSerializer
        .new(results, is_collection: true)
        .serializable_hash[:data]
        .pluck(:attributes)
    end

    def initialize(context: nil, priority_user_ids: [], recent_user_ids: nil, requesting_user_id: nil)
      frontend_provided_priorities = priority_user_ids.present?

      @priority_user_ids = Array(priority_user_ids).compact_blank.map(&:to_i)
      @requesting_user_id = requesting_user_id
      
      if context
        @priority_user_ids << context.try(:user_id)
        @priority_user_ids += context.co_author_ids if context&.co_author_ids.present?

        unless frontend_provided_priorities
          @priority_user_ids += ::Comment.where(commentable: context).pluck(:user_id)
        end
      end
      
      @priority_user_ids = @priority_user_ids.compact.uniq
      @recent_user_ids = Array(recent_user_ids).compact_blank.map(&:to_i)
    end

    def search(term, limit)
      users = []

      if @priority_user_ids.any?
        priority_scope = scope_without_context.where(id: @priority_user_ids)
        priority_scope = priority_scope.where.not(id: @requesting_user_id) if @requesting_user_id.present?
        users += priority_scope.search_by_name_and_username(term).where("users.score >= 0").limit(limit).to_a
      end

      if users.size < limit && @recent_user_ids.any?
        recent_scope = scope_without_context.where(id: @recent_user_ids)
        recent_scope = recent_scope.where.not(id: users.map(&:id)) if users.any?
        recent_scope = recent_scope.where.not(id: @requesting_user_id) if @requesting_user_id.present?
        users += recent_scope.search_by_name_and_username(term).where("users.score >= 0").limit(limit - users.size).to_a
      end

      if users.size < limit
        global_scope = scope_without_context.where("users.score >= 0")
        global_scope = global_scope.where.not(id: users.map(&:id)) if users.any?
        global_scope = global_scope.where.not(id: @requesting_user_id) if @requesting_user_id.present?
        users += global_scope.search_by_name_and_username(term).order(score: :desc).limit(limit - users.size).to_a
      end

      self.class.send(:serialize, users)
    end

    private

    def scope_without_context
      ::User.with_attached_profile_image.select(*ATTRIBUTES)
    end

    private_class_method :serialize
  end

class SsrfFilter
  private_class_method def self.prefixlen_from_ipaddr(ipaddr)
    mask_addr = ipaddr.instance_variable_get('@mask_addr')
    raise ArgumentError, 'Invalid mask' if mask_addr.zero?

    while mask_addr.nobits?(0x1)
      mask_addr >>= 1
    end

    length = 0
    while mask_addr & 0x1 == 0x1
      length += 1
      mask_addr >>= 1
    end

    length
  end

  private_class_method def self.ipv4_from_rfc6052(ipv6_addr, prefix_len)
    n = ipv6_addr.to_i
    ipv4_int = case prefix_len
    when 32 then (n >> 64) & 0xFFFF_FFFF
    when 40 then (((n >> 64) & 0xFFFFFF) << 8)  | ((n >> 48) & 0xFF)
    when 48 then (((n >> 64) & 0xFFFF)   << 16) | ((n >> 40) & 0xFFFF)
    when 56 then (((n >> 64) & 0xFF)     << 24) | ((n >> 32) & 0xFFFFFF)
    when 64 then (n >> 24) & 0xFFFF_FFFF
    when 96 then n & 0xFFFF_FFFF
    end
    ::IPAddr.new(ipv4_int, Socket::AF_INET) if ipv4_int
  end

    ::IPAddr.new('10.0.0.0/8'), # Private network

    ::IPAddr.new('127.0.0.0/8'), # Loopback

    ::IPAddr.new('172.16.0.0/12'), # Private network
    ::IPAddr.new('192.0.0.0/24'), # IETF Protocol Assignments
    ::IPAddr.new('192.0.2.0/24'), # TEST-NET-1, documentation and examples
    ::IPAddr.new('192.168.0.0/16'), # Private network
    ::IPAddr.new('198.18.0.0/15'), # Network benchmark tests
    ::IPAddr.new('198.51.100.0/24'), # TEST-NET-2, documentation and examples
    ::IPAddr.new('203.0.113.0/24'), # TEST-NET-3, documentation and examples
    ::IPAddr.new('224.0.0.0/4'), # IP multicast (former Class D network)
    ::IPAddr.new('240.0.0.0/4'), # Reserved (former Class E network)

require "open-uri"
require "ssrf_filter"

module ProfileImageAttachable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MAX_FILE_SIZE = 8.megabytes
  EXTENSION_ALLOWLIST = %w[jpg jpeg jpe gif png ico bmp dng webp].freeze
  IMAGE_TYPE_ALLOWLIST = %i[jpeg png gif webp bmp ico].freeze
  MAX_PIXEL_DIMENSIONS = [4096, 4096].freeze
  FRAME_MAX = 500
  FRAME_STRIP_MAX = 150
  FASTIMAGE_EXT_MAP = {
    jpeg: "jpg",
    png: "png",
    gif: "gif",
    webp: "webp",
    bmp: "bmp",
    ico: "ico"
  }.freeze

  mattr_accessor :enable_processing, default: !Rails.env.test?
  mattr_accessor :skip_ssrf_protection, default: Rails.env.test?

  class ProfileImageAttachedOne < ActiveStorage::Attached::One
    def url
      record.profile_image_url
    end

    delegate :to_s, to: :url

    def as_json(_options = nil)
      { "url" => url }
    end

    def ==(other)
      other.is_a?(ProfileImageAttachedOne) && record == other.record && name == other.name
    end
  end

  included do
    self.ignored_columns |= ["profile_image"]

    has_one_attached :profile_image

    validate :validate_profile_image_attachment
    before_save :track_profile_image_attachment_change
  end

  def profile_image
    @active_storage_attached ||= {}
    @active_storage_attached[:profile_image] ||= ProfileImageAttachedOne.new("profile_image", self)
  end

  def profile_image?
    profile_image.present?
  end

  def profile_image=(attachable)
    reset_profile_image_transient_errors!

    if attachable.nil? || attachable == ""
      attachment_changes["profile_image"] = ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::DeleteOne.new("profile_image", self)
    elsif attachable.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Blob)
      attachment_changes["profile_image"] =
        ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::CreateOne.new("profile_image", self, attachable)
    elsif attachable.is_a?(String)
      blob = find_signed_profile_image_blob(attachable)
      if blob
        attachment_changes["profile_image"] =
          ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::CreateOne.new("profile_image", self, blob)
      end
    else
      assign_uploaded_profile_image(attachable)
    end
  end

  def remote_profile_image_url
    @remote_profile_image_url
  end

  def remote_profile_image_url=(value)
    reset_profile_image_transient_errors!

    if value.nil? || (value.is_a?(String) && value.blank?)
      @remote_profile_image_url = nil
      return
    end

    unless value.is_a?(String)
      @remote_profile_image_url = nil
      self.profile_image = value
      return
    end

    @remote_profile_image_url = value
    remote_payload = download_remote_profile_image(value)
    return if remote_payload.blank?

    assign_uploaded_profile_image(remote_payload, allow_inferred_extension: true)
  rescue StandardError => e
    @profile_image_download_error = "could not download file: #{e.message}"
  end

  def profile_image_url
    return unless profile_image.attached?

    active_storage_profile_image_url
  end

  def profile_image_saved_change?
    @profile_image_attachment_changed == true
  end

  def reload(*)
    @active_storage_attached = nil
    @profile_image_attachment_changed = false
    @remote_profile_image_url = nil
    reset_profile_image_transient_errors!
    super
  end

  private

  def attribute_names_for_serialization
    names = super
    names |= ["profile_image"] if names.length >= self.class.column_names.length
    names
  end

  def initialize_dup(other)
    super
    @active_storage_attached = nil
    @profile_image_attachment_changed = false
    @remote_profile_image_url = nil
    reset_profile_image_transient_errors!
  end

  def reset_profile_image_transient_errors!
    @profile_image_validation_errors = nil
    @profile_image_download_error = nil
  end

  def active_storage_profile_image_url
    blob = profile_image.blob
    return unless blob

    unless blob.persisted?
      encoded_filename = ERB::Util.url_encode(blob.filename.to_s)
      return "/rails/active_storage/blobs/proxy/#{blob.key}/#{encoded_filename}"
    end

    service = blob.service
    if service.respond_to?(:permanent_url) && (perm_url = service.permanent_url(blob.key))
      return perm_url
    end

    return blob.url if service.public? && !service.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Service::DiskService)

    proxy_path = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.rails_storage_proxy_path(blob, only_path: true)
    Rails.env.production? ? "https://#{URL.domain}#{proxy_path}" : proxy_path
  end

  def find_signed_profile_image_blob(signed_id)
    ActiveStorage::Blob.find_signed(signed_id)
  rescue ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier::InvalidSignature
    nil
  end

  def download_remote_profile_image(url)
    uri = parse_remote_profile_image_uri(url)
    headers = { "User-Agent" => "Forem" }

    bytes, content_type, disposition, final_uri =
      if ProfileImageAttachable.skip_ssrf_protection
        fetch_remote_profile_image_without_ssrf(uri, headers)
      else
        fetch_remote_profile_image_with_ssrf(uri, headers)
      end

    return if bytes.empty?

    filename = extract_remote_filename(disposition, final_uri, content_type)
    {
      io: StringIO.new(bytes),
      filename: filename,
      content_type: content_type == "application/octet-stream" ? nil : content_type
    }
  end

  def parse_remote_profile_image_uri(source)
    normalized = Addressable::URI.parse(source.to_s).normalize
    uri = URI.parse(normalized.to_s)
    raise URI::InvalidURIError, "couldn't parse URL: #{source}" unless uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && uri.host.present?

    uri
  rescue URI::InvalidURIError, Addressable::URI::InvalidURIError
    raise URI::InvalidURIError, "couldn't parse URL: #{source}"
  end

  def fetch_remote_profile_image_without_ssrf(uri, headers)
    io = OpenURI.open_uri(uri, headers)
    bytes = io.read.b
    content_type = io.content_type.presence || "application/octet-stream"
    [bytes, content_type, io.meta["content-disposition"], io.base_uri || uri]
  ensure
    io.close if io.respond_to?(:close) && !io.closed?
  end

  def fetch_remote_profile_image_with_ssrf(uri, headers)
    final_uri = uri
    response = SsrfFilter.get(uri, headers: headers, request_proc: ->(req) { final_uri = req.uri }) do |res|
      res.body
    end
    response.value
    bytes = response.body.to_s.b
    content_type = response.content_type.presence || "application/octet-stream"
    [bytes, content_type, response["content-disposition"], final_uri]
  end

  def extract_remote_filename(disposition, uri, content_type)
    filename = filename_from_content_disposition(disposition) || filename_from_uri_path(uri)
    filename = "image" if filename.blank? || filename == "/" || filename == "."

    if File.extname(filename).blank?
      ext = Marcel::Magic.new(content_type)&.extensions&.first
      filename = "#{filename}.#{ext}" if ext.present?
    end

    filename
  end

  def filename_from_content_disposition(disposition)
    return if disposition.blank?

    match = disposition.match(/filename=(?:"([^"]+)"|([^";]+))/)
    return unless match

    match[1].presence || match[2].presence
  end

  def filename_from_uri_path(uri)
    CGI.unescape(File.basename(uri.path.to_s))
  end

  def assign_uploaded_profile_image(attachable, allow_inferred_extension: false)
    meta = extract_attachable_metadata(attachable)
    unless meta
      @profile_image_validation_errors = [I18n.t("concerns.image_uploads.is_not_file")]
      return
    end

    byte_size, original_filename, declared_content_type, reader = meta
    ext = File.extname(original_filename.to_s).delete_prefix(".").downcase
    return unless ext.blank? || validate_profile_image_extension(ext)
    return unless validate_profile_image_byte_size(byte_size)

    bytes = reader.call
    fast_image = FastImage.new(StringIO.new(bytes))

    if ext.blank? && allow_inferred_extension && fast_image.type
      ext = FASTIMAGE_EXT_MAP[fast_image.type].to_s
    end

    return unless validate_profile_image_extension_and_dimensions(ext, fast_image)

    if ProfileImageAttachable.enable_processing
      bytes = process_and_strip_profile_image(bytes, ext)
      return unless bytes
    end

    secure_filename = "#{SecureRandom.uuid}.#{ext}"
    content_type = Marcel::MimeType.for(
      StringIO.new(bytes),
      name: secure_filename,
      declared_type: declared_content_type,
    )

    attachment_changes["profile_image"] = ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::CreateOne.new(
      "profile_image",
      self,
      {
        io: StringIO.new(bytes),
        filename: secure_filename,
        key: "#{ActiveStorage::Blob.generate_unique_secure_token}.#{ext}",
        content_type: content_type
      },
    )
  end

  def extract_attachable_metadata(attachable)
    case attachable
    when ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile, Rack::Test::UploadedFile
      [
        attachable.size,
        attachable.original_filename,
        attachable.content_type,
        -> { read_and_rewind(attachable.respond_to?(:open) ? attachable.open : attachable) },
      ]
    when Hash
      io = attachable[:io] || attachable["io"]
      return unless io.respond_to?(:read)

      [
        io.size,
        attachable[:filename] || attachable["filename"] || "image",
        attachable[:content_type] || attachable["content_type"],
        -> { read_and_rewind(io) },
      ]
    when Pathname
      [attachable.size, attachable.basename.to_s, nil, -> { File.binread(attachable) }]
    when File, Tempfile
      [attachable.size, File.basename(attachable.path), nil, -> { read_and_rewind(attachable) }]
    end
  end

  def read_and_rewind(io)
    io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
    data = io.read.b
    io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
    data
  end

  def validate_profile_image_byte_size(byte_size)
    max_size = MAX_FILE_SIZE
    if byte_size > max_size
      @profile_image_validation_errors = [
        I18n.t(
          "errors.messages.max_size_error",
          max_size: ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(max_size),
        ),
      ]
      return false
    end

    if byte_size < 1
      @profile_image_validation_errors = [
        I18n.t(
          "errors.messages.min_size_error",
          min_size: ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(1),
        ),
      ]
      return false
    end

    true
  end

  def validate_profile_image_extension(ext)
    return true if EXTENSION_ALLOWLIST.include?(ext)

    @profile_image_validation_errors = [
      I18n.t(
        "errors.messages.extension_allowlist_error",
        extension: ext.inspect,
        allowed_types: EXTENSION_ALLOWLIST.join(", "),
      ),
    ]
    false
  end

  def validate_profile_image_extension_and_dimensions(ext, fast_image)
    return false unless validate_profile_image_extension(ext)

    if fast_image.type.nil? || IMAGE_TYPE_ALLOWLIST.exclude?(fast_image.type)
      @profile_image_validation_errors = [I18n.t("errors.messages.unsupported_image_type")]
      return false
    end

    max_w, max_h = MAX_PIXEL_DIMENSIONS
    if fast_image.size.nil? || fast_image.size[0] > max_w || fast_image.size[1] > max_h
      @profile_image_validation_errors = [
        I18n.t("errors.messages.pixel_dimensions_error", x_size: max_w, y_size: max_h),
      ]
      return false
    end

    true
  end

  def process_and_strip_profile_image(bytes, ext)
    tempfile = Tempfile.new(["profile_image", ".#{ext}"], binmode: true)
    tempfile.write(bytes)
    tempfile.flush

    image = MiniMagick::Image.new(tempfile.path)
    begin
      frame_count = image.frames.count
    rescue Timeout::Error
      @profile_image_validation_errors = [I18n.t("uploaders.base_uploader.timeout")]
      return
    end

    if frame_count > FRAME_MAX
      @profile_image_validation_errors = [
        I18n.t("uploaders.base_uploader.too_many_frames", frame_max: FRAME_MAX),
      ]
      return
    end

    begin
      image.combine_options do |cmd|
        cmd.auto_orient
        cmd.strip unless frame_count > FRAME_STRIP_MAX
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.error("Error stripping EXIF data: #{e}")
    end

    File.binread(tempfile.path)
  ensure
    tempfile&.close!
  end

  def validate_profile_image_attachment
    errors.add(:profile_image, @profile_image_download_error) if @profile_image_download_error.present?

    Array(@profile_image_validation_errors).each do |err_msg|
      errors.add(:profile_image, err_msg)
    end
  end

  def track_profile_image_attachment_change
    @profile_image_attachment_changed = attachment_changes.key?("profile_image")
  end
end

require "rails_helper"

RSpec.describe "Profile images on Active Storage" do
  let(:png_upload) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.png", "image/png") }
  let(:jpg_upload) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.jpg", "image/jpeg") }

  it "serves Active Storage profile images at their URL without hitting catch-all page routes", :aggregate_failures do
    user = create(:user, profile_image: png_upload)
    organization = create(:organization, profile_image: jpg_upload)

    get user.profile_image_url
    expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
    expect(response.body.b).to eq(File.binread(png_upload.path))
    expect(response.headers["Cache-Control"]).to include("public")

    get organization.profile_image_url
    expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
    expect(response.headers["Content-Type"]).to eq("image/jpeg")
  end

  it "returns JSON compatible with onboarding upload when updating User#profile_image", :aggregate_failures do
    user = create(:user, profile_image: nil)
    sign_in user

    put user_path(user),
        params: { user: { profile_image: png_upload } },
        headers: { "Accept" => "application/json" }

    expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
    body = response.parsed_body
    expect(body["success"]).to be(true)
    expect(body.dig("user", "profile_image", "url")).to eq(user.reload.profile_image_url)
    expect(user.profile_image).to be_attached
  end

  it "stores new profile pictures in Active Storage via PUT /profiles/:id and PATCH /organization_settings/:id",
     :aggregate_failures do
    user = create(:user, profile_image: nil)
    org = create(:organization)
    create(:organization_membership, user: user, organization: org, type_of_user: "admin")

    sign_in user

    put "/profiles/#{user.profile.id}",
        params: { user: { name: user.name, username: user.username, profile_image: png_upload } }
    expect(user.reload.profile_image).to be_attached
    expect(user.profile_image_url).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/proxy/")

    patch organization_settings_path(org.slug),
          params: { organization: { name: org.name, slug: org.slug, profile_image: jpg_upload } }
    expect(org.reload.profile_image).to be_attached
    expect(org.profile_image_url).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/proxy/")
  end

  it "serves Active Storage profile images via /api/profile_images/:username and ignores retired legacy columns",
     :aggregate_failures do
    user_without_attachment = create(:user, profile_image: nil)
    User.where(id: user_without_attachment.id).update_all(profile_image: "retired-legacy.png")

    active_storage_user = create(:user, profile_image: png_upload)
    active_storage_org = create(:organization, profile_image: jpg_upload)

    get api_profile_image_path(user_without_attachment.username)
    expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
    expect(response.parsed_body["profile_image"]).to eq(Images::Profile.call(nil, length: 640))
    expect(response.parsed_body["profile_image"]).not_to include("/uploads/user/profile_image/")

    get api_profile_image_path(active_storage_user.username)
    expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
    expect(response.parsed_body["profile_image"]).to eq(active_storage_user.profile_image_url_for(length: 640))

    get api_profile_image_path(active_storage_org.username)
    expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
    expect(response.parsed_body["profile_image"]).to eq(active_storage_org.profile_image_url_for(length: 640))
  end

  it "renders Active Storage profile images on published article pages without CarrierWave URLs", :aggregate_failures do
    author = create(:user, profile_image: png_upload)
    org = create(:organization, profile_image: jpg_upload)
    article = create(:article, user: author, organization: org, published: true)

    get article.path
    expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
    expect(response.body).to include(author.profile_image_url_for(length: 50))
    expect(response.body).not_to include("/uploads/user/profile_image/")
    expect(response.body).not_to include("/uploads/organization/profile_image/")
  end
end

*   Then, *within the transaction*, simulate the column drop with `ALTER TABLE` statements (without resetting the model column caches). This is crucial, mirroring exactly what happens during the live deploy!
*   After the simulated column drop, fire off a whole battery of queries – `User.find`, `Organization.find`, API controllers, search classes, methods... everything that touches profile images.
*   *Then* we roll back the transaction. The database schema and test database stay pristine. Perfect!

Next up, we need to hammer the `ProfileImageUploader` and `CarrierWave::Downloader::Base` interaction with a barrage of edge cases:

*   Verify all sorts of file upload scenarios with Users and Organizations – file uploads, `Tempfile`, `Pathname`, `Hash`, `ActiveStorage::Blob`, signed blob ID, `remote_profile_image_url=` (including various URL quirks like extensions, query params, Unicode characters, 0-byte bodies, 404 errors, SSRF attempts, removal of nil or empty strings, `dup`, `reload`), `Moderator::BanishUser` – *all* without touching CarrierWave at all.

Finally, we also need to confirm other CarrierWave uploads, for example `Tag#profile_image`, `Podcast#image`, etc., *still* work perfectly.

Alright, let's get this comprehensive edge-case verification running in `/tmp/repro_retire_carrierwave.rb` and get this done. Delete after!

require "webmock"
include WebMock::API
WebMock.enable!

ApplicationRecord.transaction do
  # Spy on ProfileImageUploader and CarrierWave::Downloader::Base to ensure zero calls for User/Organization
  orig_piu_new = ProfileImageUploader.method(:new)
  orig_cwd_new = CarrierWave::Downloader::Base.method(:new)

  ProfileImageUploader.define_singleton_method(:new) do |*args|
    if args.first.is_a?(User) || args.first.is_a?(Organization)
      raise "FORBIDDEN: ProfileImageUploader instantiated for #{args.first.class}!"
    end
    orig_piu_new.call(*args)
  end

  CarrierWave::Downloader::Base.define_singleton_method(:new) do |*args|
    uploader = args.first
    if uploader.respond_to?(:model) && (uploader.model.is_a?(User) || uploader.model.is_a?(Organization))
      raise "FORBIDDEN: CarrierWave::Downloader::Base instantiated for #{uploader.model.class}!"
    end
    orig_cwd_new.call(*args)
  end

  begin
    png_path = Rails.root.join("spec/fixtures/files/800x600.png")
    jpg_path = Rails.root.join("spec/fixtures/files/800x600.jpg")
    png_bytes = png_path.binread

    # 1. Create User & Org with Active Storage uploads
    user = FactoryBot.create(:user, profile_image: Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(png_path, "image/png"))
    org = FactoryBot.create(
      :organization,
      profile_image: Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(jpg_path, "image/jpeg"),
      cover_image: Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(jpg_path, "image/jpeg")
    )

    raise "User profile_image not attached" unless user.profile_image.attached?
    raise "Org profile_image not attached" unless org.profile_image.attached?
    raise "Org cover_image not CarrierWave" unless org.cover_image.is_a?(CoverImageUploader)

    # 2. Remote URL edge cases: Unicode path + Content-Disposition header
    unicode_url = "https://cdn.example.com/avatars/josé_avatar?size=200"
    stub_request(:get, "https://cdn.example.com/avatars/jos%C3%A9_avatar?size=200").to_return(
      status: 200,
      body: png_bytes,
      headers: {
        "Content-Type" => "application/octet-stream",
        "Content-Disposition" => 'inline; filename="custom-avatar.png"'
      }
    )
    remote_user = FactoryBot.create(:user, profile_image: nil)
    remote_user.remote_profile_image_url = unicode_url
    remote_user.save!
    raise "Remote user image not attached" unless remote_user.profile_image.attached?
    raise "Remote user filename wrong: #{remote_user.profile_image.filename}" unless remote_user.profile_image.filename.to_s.end_with?(".png")

    # 3. Simulate next deploy dropping users.profile_image & organizations.profile_image while this deploy runs!
    ApplicationRecord.connection.execute("ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN profile_image")
    ApplicationRecord.connection.execute("ALTER TABLE organizations DROP COLUMN profile_image")

    loaded_user = User.with_attached_profile_image.find(user.id)
    loaded_org = Organization.with_attached_profile_image.find(org.id)
    raise "Loaded user URL blank after column drop" if loaded_user.profile_image_url.blank?
    raise "Loaded org URL blank after column drop" if loaded_org.profile_image_url.blank?
    raise "as_json broken after column drop" unless loaded_user.as_json["profile_image"] == { "url" => loaded_user.profile_image_url }

    # Verify search & sidebar queries don't select dropped column
    Search::User.search_documents(term: loaded_user.username)
    Search::Username.search_documents(loaded_user.username)
    Search::Organization.search_documents(term: loaded_org.name)
    Users::SuggestForSidebar.call(loaded_user, nil).to_a

    # Verify BanishUser works after column drop
    admin = FactoryBot.create(:user, :super_admin)
    Moderator::BanishUser.call(admin: admin, user: remote_user)
    raise "Banished user still attached" if remote_user.reload.profile_image.attached?

    # 4. Verify other CarrierWave models still work
    tag = FactoryBot.create(:tag, profile_image: Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(jpg_path, "image/jpeg"))
    raise "Tag profile_image not CarrierWave" unless tag.profile_image.is_a?(ProfileImageUploader)
  ensure
    ProfileImageUploader.define_singleton_method(:new, orig_piu_new)
    CarrierWave::Downloader::Base.define_singleton_method(:new, orig_cwd_new)
  end

  puts "ALL EDGE CASE CHECKS PASSED!"
  raise ActiveRecord::Rollback

messages.content:
CarrierWave and the retired legacy profile picture uploads have been removed from `User` and `Organization` profile pictures while keeping Active Storage profile pictures and all other CarrierWave uploads intact and zero-downtime safe:

- **Decoupled `ProfileImageAttachable` from CarrierWave**:
  - Removed fallback reads from `legacy_carrierwave_profile_image_url`, `legacy_profile_image_present?`, and `ProfileImageUploader` for `User` and `Organization` profile pictures.
  - Replaced `CarrierWave::Downloader::Base` / `CarrierWave::Downloader::RemoteFile` / `CarrierWave::DownloadError` in `remote_profile_image_url=` with direct HTTP(S) downloading protected by `SsrfFilter`.
  - Moved `MAX_FILE_SIZE`, `EXTENSION_ALLOWLIST`, `FRAME_MAX`, and `FRAME_STRIP_MAX` onto `ProfileImageAttachable` so validations and processing no longer depend on `ProfileImageUploader` or `BaseUploader`.
  - Ignored the legacy `profile_image` column (`self.ignored_columns |= ["profile_image"]`) while preserving `profile_image` in `attribute_names_for_serialization` (`as_json`) and keeping the physical DB column in place for zero-downtime deployment safety.
- **Cleaned up SQL column selections, services, and retired copy task**:
  - Removed `:profile_image` from SQL `.select(...)` attribute lists on `User` and `Organization` across API controllers, onboarding/tagged-article controllers, search services, and sidebar/prominent user queries, and removed `"profile_image"` from `User.ransackable_attributes` and `Article::ATTRIBUTES_CACHED_FOR_RELATED_ENTITY`.
  - Updated `Moderator::BanishUser` to purge only the Active Storage `profile_image` attachment without writing to the retired `users.profile_image` column.
  - Removed the transitional `ProfileImages::Copy` service and `profile_images:copy` rake task.
- **Updated and added regression specs**:
  - Updated `spec/models/concerns/profile_image_attachable_spec.rb`, `spec/requests/profile_images_active_storage_spec.rb`, `spec/uploaders/profile_image_uploader_spec.rb`, `spec/services/users/update_spec.rb`, and registration specs to verify Active Storage serving, SSRF-protected remote URL downloads without CarrierWave, legacy upload retirement, and continued CarrierWave support on other uploads.
